input:
Before the strainer cleaning can begin, the duty has to be
transferred in an orderly fashion. The transfer begins by starting
the standby pump, and once it is delivering steadily, the duty
pump can be stopped. The strainer outlet valve is then closed, followed by the
strainer inlet valve, so that the strainer body is separated from
the line on both sides. Because the strainer serves the suction of
the duty pump, its starter is locked under the PTW, so that the
pump cannot be started against a blanked suction path, and the
control room is informed which pump is now the running machine.

The strainer vent and drain are opened so that the body can drain
into the closed drain, and the vent is left open while draining is
in progress, with time allowed for the element to drip dry.

A point calling for care is that stored pressure can remain held
in the strainer body, trapped behind a fouled element, even after
the body has been vented. The body is therefore proved to be at
atmospheric pressure by its test point, and the drain checked to
have stopped running, before the cover is slackened.

The isolation is then recorded on the PTW in the order in which it
was made. With the strainer isolated, drained and proved in this
condition, the cleaning and refitting that follow take about
65 min.
target:
Transfer the duty to the standby pump before the strainer is
touched. Start it, prove that it is delivering steadily, and stop
the duty pump.
Close the strainer outlet valve, and then the strainer inlet valve,
so that the strainer body is separated from the line on both sides.
Lock the duty pump starter under the PTW, since the strainer serves
the suction of the duty pump and the pump must not be started
against a blanked suction path. Tell the control room which pump is
now the running machine.

Open the strainer vent and the strainer drain, and drain the body
to the closed drain. Leave the vent open while the body drains, and
allow time for the element to drip dry into the body.

Stored pressure can be held in the strainer body behind a fouled
element after the body has been vented. Prove the body at
atmospheric pressure at the test point, and check that the drain
has stopped running, before the cover is slackened.

Record the isolation on the PTW in the order in which it was made.
With the strainer isolated, drained and proved in this condition,
the cleaning and refitting that follow take about 65 min.
